q: A salary bill for a division has been prepared and passed at the unit level. For the monthly account, the compiled expenditure position against the budget grant has to be viewed by the finance officer. The correct system/stage for this compiled view is:

options.A: RESS, through the employee self-service window
options.B: IPAS, for preparing a fresh pay bill
options.C: AIMS, as the compilation and management reporting layer

e: IPAS handles working-level payroll and bill transactions; AIMS compiles the accounts data and presents expenditure, earnings and suspense positions for management review.

q: A newly appointed employee's particulars are to be entered so that salary can be drawn for the first time. Before the employee becomes payable in the payroll system, the entry must be:

options.A: Approved by the depot storekeeper in iMMS
options.B: Entered directly by any dealing clerk without verification
options.C: Confirmed through the UMID medical card registration
options.D: Verified and confirmed by the Establishment section of the Accounts Department in IPAS

e: A new employee cannot simply be added to IPAS; the entry requires verification/confirmation by the Establishment section of Accounts, which checks the appointment particulars first.

q: During internal check of a pay bill, an increment event recorded for an employee appears doubtful. Since pay particulars flow into the bill from the service master, the check should begin with:

options.A: The bank scroll for the month
options.B: The HRMS electronic service record (e-SR) event
options.C: The GeM order for office supplies

e: IPAS draws pay particulars from the HRMS master, so a wrong appointment date, level or increment event in HRMS/e-SR becomes a wrong salary bill; internal check of pay begins with the HRMS event.

q: A pensioner's pension has to be revised following implementation of a pay commission's recommendations, instead of recalculating every Pension Payment Order manually. This revision processing is carried out through:
e: ARPAN is the portal through which pension revision on pay commission implementation and pension-related processing is carried out for railway pensioners.

q: An employee reports to a railway hospital away from his home station for treatment of an eligible dependant. The identity that establishes medical entitlement at the hospital counter is carried through:

options.C: The pay slip viewed in RESS
options.D: The DSC token used for tendering

e: UMID is the Unique Medical Identity card issued to serving employees, pensioners and eligible dependants, identifying the beneficiary for railway medical facilities across hospitals.

q: A file containing a sanction that supports a payment has to move from the dealing assistant to the approving officer, and at audit the office must show who noted on it and when. This file movement and its audit trail are provided by:
e: e-Office moves files, receipts and noting electronically; every movement is logged, so who noted, who approved and when forms part of the voucher's evidence.

q: Earnings cash remittance details entered in the accounts system for a station do not agree with the freight operations figures for the same period. The reconciliation to be performed is between:

options.A: E-CR details in IPAS and figures in FOIS
options.B: APAR in HRMS and pension data in ARPAN
options.C: Stock in UDM and orders on GeM
options.D: Files in e-Office and tenders in IREPS

e: The note specifically provides that E-CR details entered in the IPAS module are reconciled with the figures appearing in FOIS, and differences are a standard internal-check item.

q: An employee wants to see his own pay slip and service particulars without visiting the establishment section. The self-service window provided for this purpose is:
e: RESS, the Railway Employee Self Service portal/app, lets an employee view his own pay slips and service particulars, reducing counter work in the establishment section.

q: One railway has executed work on behalf of another railway and raised a transfer advice. The respondent railway finds the advice in order. For the transfer transaction to be complete under e-Recon, the respondent railway must:

options.A: Ignore the advice, as electronic advices need no response
options.C: Record its acceptance of the advice in e-Recon
options.D: Refer the advice to the paying bank

e: Acceptance remains necessary under e-Recon; the originating railway raises the advice and the transaction is complete only when the respondent railway accepts it, with unmatched items monitored online.

q:
Consider the following statements about IPAS and AIMS:
1. IPAS processes payroll and day-to-day accounting transactions at the unit/division level.
2. AIMS has replaced IPAS for preparation of salary bills.
3. AIMS provides consolidated views of expenditure against budget grant, earnings and suspense balances.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. AIMS is the information and reporting layer built on accounts data; it has not replaced IPAS, which remains the transaction and payroll engine.

q:
Consider the following statements about HRMS:
1. The service record of an employee is maintained electronically as e-SR in HRMS.
2. The APAR workflow of self-appraisal, reporting, reviewing and acceptance is carried out in HRMS.
3. Salary bills are passed and paid directly in HRMS.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: HRMS holds the employee master, e-SR and the APAR workflow; payroll processing and bill passing take place in IPAS, which draws particulars from HRMS.

q:
Consider the following statements about e-Recon:
1. It is the electronic system for reconciliation of inter-railway transfer transactions.
2. Under e-Recon, acceptance of a transfer advice by the respondent railway is no longer necessary.
3. It enables online monitoring of transfer transactions that remain unmatched or unaccepted.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The claim that acceptance is no longer necessary is a known trap; acceptance by the respondent railway is still required.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. UMID cards are issued only to railway pensioners.
2. Purchase Suspense figures come under a module of IPAS.
3. Most railway applications are designed and maintained by CRIS.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
e: UMID covers serving employees, pensioners and eligible family members/dependants, so statement 1 is wrong. Purchase Suspense figures under an IPAS module, and CRIS is the Railways' IT organisation maintaining most applications.

q: In the digital workflow of the Railways, day-to-day payroll processing and passing of bills at the unit/division level are carried out in:
e: IPAS is the integrated application through which payroll and day-to-day accounting work, including passing of bills, is processed at the unit/division level.

q: The Annual Performance Appraisal Report (APAR) workflow for railway employees is carried out online in:
e: Self-appraisal, reporting, reviewing and acceptance of APAR are carried out online in HRMS, and APAR grading is what the MACPS benchmark is judged on.

q: Pension revision and pension-related processing for railway pensioners are carried out through the portal named:
e: ARPAN is the portal for revision of pension/family pension, prominently on pay commission implementation, and for pension-related processing.

q: The in-house data communication network (intranet) of Indian Railways on which internal communication runs is:
e: Internal communication across the Railways runs on Railnet, the in-house data communication network of Indian Railways.

q: Freight earnings of the Railways originate as system data in:
e: Goods booking, freight calculation and terminal collections run on FOIS, so freight earnings originate in FOIS and Traffic Accounts checks run on FOIS data.

q: Timely acceptance and clearance of transfer transactions under e-Recon helps to keep clean, at the close of accounts, the balances under:
e: Clearance of transfer transactions keeps the Transfer Divisional / Transfer Railways balances clean at the close of accounts.

q: Which of the following statements about the IPAS–AIMS relationship is NOT correct?

options.A: IPAS is the transaction and payroll engine at the working level
options.B: AIMS is the accounting information and management reporting layer
options.C: AIMS has replaced IPAS, which is no longer used for payroll
options.D: Monthly and annual account figures flow from the transaction systems into the reporting layer

e: IPAS and AIMS are not rivals and neither has replaced the other: IPAS does payroll and working-level transactions, AIMS reports on the accounts data.

q: Which of the following is NOT a function or content of HRMS?

options.A: Maintenance of the electronic service record (e-SR)

e: Scrap sale by e-auction is an IREPS function. HRMS covers the employee lifecycle: e-SR, APAR and leave/pass/establishment workflows.

q: Which of the following statements about UMID is NOT correct?

options.A: It is the portal through which pension revision is processed
options.B: It is a smart health card initiative of Indian Railways
options.C: It is issued to serving employees, pensioners and eligible dependants
options.D: It identifies the beneficiary for availing railway medical facilities

e: Pension revision is processed through ARPAN. UMID is a medical identity system only — not a pension portal, salary software or booking system.

q: Which of the following statements about e-Office is NOT correct?

options.A: Files, receipts and noting move electronically in e-Office
options.B: Every movement of a file in e-Office is logged, creating an audit trail
options.C: e-Office is the system in which salary bills are prepared and passed
options.D: Sanctions and correspondence supporting a payment may travel through e-Office

e: Salary bills are prepared and passed in IPAS. e-Office concerns files and correspondence; it is not a payroll system, tendering system or accounting ledger.

q: Which of the following statements about digital payment discipline in railway offices is NOT correct?

options.A: A suspicious transaction or an unrecognised login must be reported immediately through the office channel
options.B: A transaction done with an officer's login is treated as done by that officer
options.C: A change of an employee's or vendor's bank account in the master must be independently verified
options.D: Passwords and DSC PINs may be shared with a trusted colleague for urgent work

e: Credentials are personal and must never be shared; a transaction done with one's login or DSC is treated as one's own act. The other statements state correct cyber-security discipline.

q:
Assertion (A): Internal check of a pay bill should begin with the HRMS/e-SR event rather than with the bill itself.
Reason (R): IPAS draws pay particulars from the HRMS master, so an error in the HRMS service event flows into the salary bill.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R correctly explains A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

e: Both are true, and R explains A: because payroll particulars originate in the HRMS master, checking the source event is the correct starting point.

q:
Assertion (A): A new employee cannot be added to the IPAS database by any dealing clerk on his own.
Reason (R): Salary bills for a division are compiled and reported in AIMS.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R correctly explains A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

e: Both statements are true — new IPAS entries need Establishment (Accounts) verification, and AIMS does compile/report accounts — but the AIMS role does not explain the entry control in IPAS.

q:
Assertion (A): Under e-Recon, a transfer transaction is complete as soon as the originating railway raises the electronic advice.
Reason (R): e-Recon provides online monitoring of transfer transactions that remain unmatched or unaccepted.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R correctly explains A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

e: A is false: acceptance by the respondent railway is still necessary. R is true: e-Recon monitors unmatched/unaccepted items online.

q:
Assertion (A): Differences between E-CR details entered in IPAS and FOIS figures are a standard internal-check item.
Reason (R): IPAS figures must agree with the originating operational system, and E-CR details are reconciled with FOIS.

options.A: Both A and R are true and R correctly explains A
options.B: Both A and R are true but R does not explain A
options.C: A is true but R is false
options.D: A is false but R is true

e: Both are true and R correctly explains A: the E-CR entry in IPAS is reconciled against FOIS, so any difference is picked up in internal check.

q:
Match the system with its primary role:
I. IPAS   II. HRMS   III. ARPAN   IV. UMID
a. Pension revision and pension processing
b. Payroll and accounting transactions at unit level
c. Medical identity of employees, pensioners and dependants
d. Employee lifecycle records and e-service record
e: IPAS = payroll/accounting transactions; HRMS = lifecycle records and e-SR; ARPAN = pension; UMID = medical identity.

q:
Match the system with its primary role:
I. AIMS   II. e-Office   III. e-Recon   IV. FOIS
a. Paperless movement of files and noting
b. Compilation and management reporting of accounts
c. Freight operations and goods earnings data
d. Reconciliation of inter-railway transfer transactions
e: AIMS reports accounts; e-Office moves files; e-Recon reconciles transfer transactions; FOIS runs freight operations.

q:
Match the workflow stage with the system in which it occurs:
I. Employee master and service events recorded   II. Pay bill prepared and passed   III. Payment made to employee/vendor   IV. Accounts compiled and reported
a. Bank, against payment advice
b. HRMS
c. AIMS
d. IPAS
e: The chain runs HRMS (master) → IPAS (bill passed) → Bank (payment) → AIMS (compilation and reporting).

q:
Match the item with the system that holds or processes it:
I. e-SR   II. APAR workflow   III. Purchase Suspense figures   IV. Pay slip view by the employee himself
a. IPAS module
b. HRMS
c. HRMS
d. RESS
e: The e-SR and the APAR workflow both live in HRMS; Purchase Suspense figures come under an IPAS module; an employee views his own pay slip through RESS.

q:
Match the system with its user or beneficiary:
I. UMID   II. ARPAN   III. RESS   IV. e-Recon
a. Accounts offices of two railways settling transfer claims
b. Railway pensioners whose pension is revised/processed
c. Serving employees, pensioners and dependants seeking medical care
d. Employees viewing their own pay and service particulars
e: UMID serves medical beneficiaries; ARPAN serves pensioners; RESS serves employees themselves; e-Recon serves accounts offices reconciling transfer transactions.

q:
Match the control or check with the system concerned:
I. Verification of a new employee's appointment particulars before pay   II. Reconciliation of E-CR details with operations figures   III. Monitoring of unaccepted transfer advices   IV. Checking pension debits against PPO and revision authority
a. e-Recon
b. Establishment section in IPAS
c. IPAS with FOIS
d. ARPAN-based pension processing
e: New-employee verification is an IPAS/Establishment control; E-CR is reconciled IPAS–FOIS; unaccepted advices are monitored in e-Recon; pension debits are checked against PPO/ARPAN revision.

q:
Match the system with the family it belongs to:
I. IPAS   II. HRMS   III. FOIS   IV. e-Office
a. Personnel
b. Office and reconciliation
c. Pay and accounts
d. Operations
e: IPAS is pay & accounts; HRMS is personnel; FOIS is operations; e-Office belongs to the office & reconciliation family.

q:
Match the function with the correct system:
I. Viewing expenditure against budget grant as a dashboard   II. Recording a transfer/promotion event   III. Revising family pension on pay commission implementation   IV. Answering 'where is the file?' from a movement log
a. HRMS
b. e-Office
c. AIMS
d. ARPAN
e: Budget-linked consolidated views are AIMS; service events are HRMS; pension revision is ARPAN; file tracking is e-Office.

q:
Match the sub-system or record with its parent system:
I. TMS (terminal working)   II. e-SR   III. Rake Management System (RMS)   IV. Coaching Operations Information System (COIS)
a. HRMS
b. FOIS
c. FOIS
d. Operations information family
e: TMS is the operating core of FOIS and RMS handles rake information in the FOIS family; the e-SR is maintained in HRMS; COIS belongs to the operations information family.

q:
Match the statement with the system it correctly describes:
I. 'Holds the man' — employee master and lifecycle   II. 'Pays the man and books the money'   III. 'Reports the money'   IV. 'Settles claims between railways'
a. IPAS
b. e-Recon
c. HRMS
d. AIMS
e: The one-line map in the note: HRMS holds the man, IPAS pays the man and books the money, AIMS reports the money, e-Recon settles claims between railways.

q:
Match the item with the system:
I. Digital life certificate keeping a pensioner on the payment roll   II. Family composition recorded for medical entitlement   III. Drawings approved digitally on the works side   IV. Management of passenger coaches
a. UMID
b. Pension payment system linked with ARPAN
c. ICMS
d. e-DAS
e: Life-certificate processes keep the pensioner on the roll in the pension system; family composition for medical entitlement is in UMID; drawing approval is e-DAS; coach management is ICMS.

q:
Match the risk or duty with the correct digital practice:
I. Change of vendor's bank account in the master   II. Use of DSC token on a procurement portal   III. Carrying payroll data on a personal pen drive   IV. Mail asking to 'verify' credentials through a link
a. Prohibited — official data stays on official systems and devices
b. Treat as phishing — verify through the official channel, not the link
c. Independent verification is compulsory
d. Keep in personal custody — the DSC is the signer's legal signature
e: Bank-detail changes need independent verification; the DSC stays in personal custody as a legal signature; payroll data must not go on personal devices; credential-verification mails are phishing.
